title: Supply Chain Infiltration in Nigeria’s Alcoholic Beverage Sector: Mapping Illicit Network Structures and Downstream Vulnerabilities
summary: Background: Counterfeit alcoholic beverages pose a major public health threat in Nigeria, yet their infiltration of legitimate supply chains remains poorly understood, especially in Sub-Saharan African markets where informality and weak regulation create conditions overlooked by mainstream counterfeiting models. Methods: This study utilised a qualitative multiple case design, drawing on eight enforcement cases and fourteen semi-structured interviews with retailers, distributors, regulatory officers and police. Results: The findings revealed a contradiction to global models built on the model of upstream adulteration or transnational smuggling. The findings revealed that counterfeiting in Nigeria operates domestically, whereby the supply chain is vertically compressed network in which manufacturing, warehousing, distribution and retail are operated as whole within residential and commercial premises. Three operational clusters are identified: vertically integrated illicit hubs (Cluster A), covert urban micro-production sites (Cluster B), and peripheral component and distribution nodes (Cluster C). Conclusions: Theoretically, the study extends Transaction Cost Economics by showing illicit actors invert conventional governance logic to minimise detection rather than transaction costs; enriches Principal–Agent Theory by demonstrating dual-agency equilibria in which downstream intermediaries serve legitimate and illicit principals simultaneously; and integrates institutional voids theory to explain why this infiltration regime self-reinforces under fragmented licensing and sporadic enforcement.

title: Digital transformation and dynamic capabilities for sustainable sme advantage: Business model innovation mediation
summary: SMEs increasingly adopt digital technologies, yet adoption alone does not ensure sustainable competitive advantage. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, the resource-based view, and business model innovation literature, this study examines how digital transformation and dynamic capabilities relate to perceived sustainable competitive advantage through business model innovation. Using survey data from 400 SMEs in West Sumatra, Indonesia, the model was tested with PLS-SEM and robustness controls for firm age and size. The results show that digital transformation and dynamic capabilities positively relate to business model innovation and competitive advantage. Business model innovation is the strongest predictor, while dynamic capabilities have a larger total effect than digital transformation. Business model innovation partially mediates both relationships, and the results remain stable after controls. These findings show that SME competitiveness is capability-enabled and business-model-mediated, implying that support programs should extend beyond technology adoption toward capability development, business model renewal, and measurable competitive outcomes.

title: Digital Transformation and Academic Library Serviceability in State-Owned Universities in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
summary: Digital transformation is redefining how academic libraries acquire, organise, preserve and deliver information. In Nigerian state-owned universities, however, the conversion of isolated technologies into dependable, user-centred services remains uneven. This study examined the influence of digital transformation on academic library serviceability in the three state-owned universities in Bayelsa State: Niger Delta University, University of Africa, Toru-Orua, and Bayelsa Medical University. Digital transformation was operationalised through three dimensions: digital infrastructure adequacy, librarians' digital competence, and digital service integration. A correlational survey design was adopted. Because the article is a methodological demonstration rather than a report of completed fieldwork, a clearly labelled simulated dataset of 240 valid library-user responses was generated to reflect plausible response patterns across the three institutions. The Digital Transformation and Library Serviceability Questionnaire contained 24 items measured on a four-point scale. Simulated reliability coefficients ranged from .82 to .88. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple and multiple regression were used, and all numerical analyses are reported in tables. Results indicated moderate digital infrastructure, relatively stronger staff digital competence, moderate digital service integration and moderate-tohigh library serviceability. Digital infrastructure significantly predicted serviceability (R² = .299, β = .547, p < .001); digital competence significantly predicted serviceability (R² = .361, β = .601, p < .001); and digital service integration was the strongest bivariate predictor (R² = .443, β = .666, p < .001). Jointly, the three dimensions explained 54.8% of the simulated variance in serviceability. The study concludes that technology acquisition alone is insufficient: infrastructure must be reliable, librarians must possess applied digital capabilities, and systems must be integrated into end-to-end user journeys. Recommendations include protected digital-library funding, continuous competency-based training, unified discovery and authentication, remote reference services, accessibility standards, service analytics and institutional digitaltransformation governance. The findings are illustrative and must not be represented as observations from real participants; they provide a defensible template for a future field study in Bayelsa State.

title: Research on the correlation between enterprise scale and MSCI ESG rating: empirical evidence from global carmakers
summary: In the context of global low-carbon transition and universal standardized sustainable disclosure, ESG assessment has become a core indicator for measuring the environmental governance, social responsibility, and internal governance levels of listed manufacturers. The traditional industrial logic holds that higher revenues can provide sufficient funds for green transformation and welfare investment, thereby enhancing the MSCI ESG rating. However, existing studies lack targeted group comparisons between traditional fuel vehicle and new energy vehicle enterprises, resulting in inconsistent conclusions regarding the correlation between enterprise size and ESG performance. This paper takes 30 global leading listed automotive manufacturers as the research object, extracting raw data from the 2025 New Energy ESG Co-creation Database; using annual revenue (in units of millions of US dollars) as the proxy indicator for enterprise size, and dividing MSCI ratings into seven levels, converting them into continuous numerical scores from 1 to 7, and conducting empirical analysis through descriptive statistics, full sample Pearson correlation test, and industry heterogeneity grouping test. The Pearson correlation coefficient of the overall sample is -0.1340, indicating a weak negative correlation between the annual revenue of automotive manufacturers and the MSCI quantitative score. Subgroup data shows that the average revenue of new energy vehicle enterprises is much lower than that of traditional fuel vehicle enterprises, but their average ESG score is significantly higher; the hierarchical sample sorting verifies the nonlinear reverse rule: enterprises with AAA ratings have the smallest average operating scale, while enterprises with A ratings have the largest revenue scale. Further mechanism analysis indicates that the core production direction of the enterprise (fuel vehicle or new energy vehicle business) rather than the absolute revenue scale is the key factor affecting MSCI performance. Based on all the above empirical results, this paper proposes differentiated operational strategies for automotive manufacturers, provides targeted rule optimization suggestions for third-party rating agencies such as MSCI, and formulates supportive regulatory policies for the national carbon peak and carbon neutrality authorities.

title: AI and Digital Transformation in the Renewable Energy Sector: A Strategic Framework for Sustainable Business Performance
summary: Purpose: The global shift towards clean energy necessitates robust business strategies to address challenges related to intermittent supply, operational inefficiencies, and evolving market conditions. This study fills a gap in strategic management literature by exploring the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Transformation (DT) in enhancing sustainable business performance within renewable energy enterprises. Design/Methodology/Approach: Utilizing the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study conducts a qualitative conceptual synthesis and systematic analysis of recent literature (2018–2026) to formulate an integrated strategic management framework. Findings: The study presents the AI-Driven Digital Transformation for Sustainable Energy (ADT-SE) framework. This model demonstrates that the alignment of technological drivers—such as predictive analytics, IoT, smart grids, and block chain—with core organizational capabilities significantly enhances financial performance, operational efficiency, and environmental stewardship. Practical Implications: The study offers renewable energy executives and policy planners a practical roadmap for capital allocation, digital risk management, and the development of cross-functional capabilities. Originality/Value: This research connects technical AI applications with corporate sustainability strategies within the Commerce and Management domain.

title: From IT-enabled organisational transformation to digital transformation: leadership strategies for value creation in manufacturing
summary: Digital Transformation (DT), which encompasses Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0, has been conceptualised and often paralleled with IT-Enabled Organizational Transformation (ITOT) by academia and practitioners. Despite their shared foundation in organisational transformation, the goals pursued are not the same, demanding different leadership profiles to either reinforce an organisation's existing value proposition and identity in ITOT or redefine its value proposition and establish a new organisational identity in DT. This paper aims to identify leadership strategies supporting value creation within organisations through the ITOT and DT journeys, including leadership competencies and practices related to the organisation's purpose with digital initiatives. This research employed a Fuzzy Delphi method based on a survey of 46 leaders involved in ITOT or DT in manufacturing companies in Brazil. Our findings reveal that leaders consider themselves mostly unprepared to navigate these organisational transformations in the manufacturing sector. The study highlights the need for leaders to create value beyond technological aspects and embrace a human-centric approach to change management that enables strategic organisational transformation. Our main contribution is a framework guiding the alignment between leadership strategies and competencies development to support ITOT and DT according to the organisation's purpose to become more sensing, smart, sustainable or social.

title: Bibliometric analysis of research trends in digital transformation and mental health from 2014 to 2024
summary: Abstract Digital transformation has significantly reshaped modern society, with important implications for mental health. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution, main contributors, and thematic development of research on digital transformation and its psychological effects. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on studies indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed databases, covering the period January 1, 2014 to June 20, 2024. A total of 2287 publications were initially identified, of which 1606 were included in the analysis. The study employed the Biblioshiny application within the Bibliometrix package in RStudio. The bibliometric approach included performance analysis (scientific production, author affiliations, most cited journals, and collaboration networks) and thematic analysis (keyword frequency, research trends over time, co-occurrence networks, longitudinal thematic evolution, and thematic maps). The analysis highlights a substantial increase in research output over the studied period and identifies key contributors and geographical patterns in the field. It reveals important gaps in the literature, particularly regarding the relationship between emerging digitalization components (e.g., remote work, Internet of Things (IoT), virtual reality, blockchain) and mental health. In addition, the findings indicate the rapid emergence of new research directions driven by technological advances, especially in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital environments. This study provides a baseline overview of the field prior to the accelerated expansion of AI-driven research observed after mid-2024. The findings have important implications for mental health research prioritization, clinical awareness, and the development of evidence-based interventions addressing the psychological impact of emerging digital technologies.

title: Climate change, ESG–based sustainability uncertainty and insurance expansion
summary: Purpose This paper aims to examine the combined effects of climate risk and environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-related uncertainty on insurance companies across a panel of 11 countries. Design/methodology/approach This study uses the annual time series data related to 11 countries, ranging from 2010 to the 2023. The authors use the panel quantile autoregressive distributed lag regression and Granger non-causality analysis techniques. Findings The findings show significant heterogeneity across quantiles in the determinants of insurance expansion. ESG-related sustainability uncertainty promotes insurance growth in the long run, especially in higher quantiles, while climate performance improves insurance revenues in the short run, mainly in lower quantiles. In contrast, climate change uncertainty has an immediate positive effect in countries with low insurance premiums, but its long-term impact diminishes in high-premium markets. These findings are consistent with stakeholder theory and institutional theory. Practical implications Climate and ESG-related sustainability uncertainty require policy frameworks that account for the unintended effects of mitigation measures on insurers’ risk assessment and pricing while ensuring the affordability of climate-related microinsurance. Integrating uncertainty into risk models and aligning insurance practices with sustainability goals improves risk estimation and enhances the long-term resilience of the insurance sector. Originality/value The authors results contribute to the existing literature on ESG and climate-related uncertainty in insurance market expansion and provide useful insights for policymakers and insurance practitioners.

title: The Effect of Profitability, Public Accounting Firm Reputation, and Firm Size on Audit Report Lag: Evidence from Property and Real Estate Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2022-2025)
summary: This study examines the effect of profitability, public accounting firm (Kantor Akuntan Publik/KAP) reputation, and firm size on audit report lag (ARL) among property and real estate companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) between 2022 and 2025. Using purposive sampling, 40 companies were selected, yielding 160 firm-year observations that were analyzed with panel data regression. The findings are interpreted through agency theory and signalling theory and suggest that higher profitability and the use of a Big Four auditor are associated with a longer, rather than a shorter, audit process plausibly because both attract more extensive audit scrutiny whereas larger firms benefit from stronger internal controls, greater resources, and closer external monitoring that shorten audit completion time.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Cybersecurity for Digital Supply Chains: A Hybrid Ensemble Approach to Real-Time Threat Detection
summary: Rapid digitalization has increased the attack surface in Supply Chain Management (SCM), making organizations highly vulnerable to emergent sophisticated cyberattacks. Traditional signature-based security remains for the most part reactive and unable to cope with fast evolving malware, phishing, ransomware, and insider intrusion. This research proposed a hybrid ensemble deep learning cybersecurity system for real-time anomaly detection within Digital Supply Chains (DSC). The existing system faced some challenges which include deficiency in both theoretical frameworks and practical solutions to proactive cyberattack detection mechanisms and inability to adapt to evolving threats in digital supply chain. The above challenges was tackled by developing a deep learning models that optimized deep learning algorithms capable of analyzing diverse data sources within the digital supply chain, including transaction records, network logs, and sensor data, to detect and mitigate cyber threats in real-time and also created an adaptive cyber security system for digital supply chain systems using deep learning algorithms capable of continuously learning from new data. Following an Agile iterative methodology for system development in six sprints involving activities on data preprocessing, classical machine learning baselines, neural network development, hybrid model integration, model evaluation, and operational deployment, using the MalwareData dataset, the best performance of 98.38% accuracy with an F1-score of 0.97 from Random Forest (RF) was obtained in comparison with 95.62% from Logistic Regression and 94.49% from the standalone Neural Network. Even more robustness with fewer false positives was exhibited with the hybrid ensemble model by amalgamating machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques in order to reinforce threat detection. Streamlit powered by SQLite has been used for deployment, rendering a responsive and user-friendly interface for real-time monitoring within simulated DSC environments. This research proposed a scalable and adaptive cybersecurity solution for modern supply chains.

title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CYBERSECURITY RISK ASSESSMENT AND AUDIT PERFORMANCE
summary: There have been transformations in business processes, accounting practices, and organisational decision making due to the rising use of digital technology. Organisational systems are prone to sophisticated cyber security threats such as ransomware attacks, phishing attacks, malware, insider threats, and unauthorized access to systems despite these technological advancements that have helped boost efficiency. These pose serious threats to the availability, confidentiality, and integrity of organisational information that will affect accounting practices and auditing. By using a comprehensive examination of the literature, auditing standards, and cybersecurity frameworks used around the world, this study aims to examine the relationship between cybersecurity risk assessment and audit performance. Cybersecurity risk assessment improves audit planning, internal control assessment, audit quality, compliance with regulations, and overall audit performance, according to the study that uses descriptive research design and qualitative content analysis on secondary sources. To improve audit performance, the study finds that cybersecurity risk assessment is now an indispensable component of auditing and recommends continuous monitoring of cybersecurity, adoption of advanced technology, and collaboration between auditors and cybersecurity professionals.

title: CEO Gender Diversity and Financial Expertise of Nigerian Oil and Gas Companies: Do They Affect Real Earnings Management?
summary: This study examined the influence of chief executive officers gender diversity and financial expertise on real earnings management of listed Nigerian oil and gas companies from 2013 to 2022. In specific, the study answered questions relating to the influence of chief executive officer gender diversity and financial expertise on real earnings management. To provide answers to the questions, secondary data were obtained for 10 listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria. Panel data regression (panel corrected standard error fixed effect model) was used because the variables of the study had time series and cross-sectional data attributes. Findings indicated that chief executive officer gender diversity and financial expertise had significant influence on real earnings management. Consequently, the study concludes that financial expertise and gender diversity are major drivers of real earnings management. On this note, the study recommends that more females should be appointed as CEO positions as they tend to reduce and avert real earnings management practices to a very large extent. Also, those that have the authority to appoint CEOs should consider people with financial expertise to emerge as CEOs

title: The Impact of Intellectual Property Protection on Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk
summary: Cybersecurity risks affect an organization's data and intangible assets, while intellectual property (IP) laws promote innovation. This study examines how corporate governance, digital transformation, and IP regulations relate to cybersecurity risk. It investigates whether stronger IP protection increases enterprise cybersecurity risk and whether network governance mediates this relationship under varying institutional enforcement. Using a two-way fixed effects regression with instrumental variables on panel data from 950 publicly listed non-financial firms across 18 countries (2012–2022; 8,547 firm-year observations), the study draws on multiple global datasets. Results show a significant positive link between IP protection intensity and cybersecurity risk (β=0.127, p < 0.01). Network governance partially mediates this relationship, reducing its impact (indirect effect=0.031). Strong institutional enforcement weakens the IP–risk link (β=-0.112, p< 0.05). The study extends appropriability theory by highlighting cybersecurity externalities of IP protection.

title: Oil Price Uncertainty, Market Fluctuations, and ESG on Energy Investment in ASEAN and East Asia
summary: Background: The energy sector is highly vulnerable to oil price uncertainty, financial market fluctuations, and sustainability demands, making investment decisions increasingly dependent on both economic factors and ESG performance. Objective: This study aims to examine the effects of oil price uncertainty, financial market fluctuations, and ESG performance on the investment policies of oil and gas companies in ASEAN and East Asia. Methods: This study employs a quantitative approach using panel data regression. The sample comprises 35 oil and gas companies listed on stock exchanges in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, China, and South Korea from 2016 to 2024, yielding 315 firm-year observations, of which 260 are available for models including ESG. Investment policy is measured using the ratio of capital expenditure to total assets. Results: Oil price uncertainty has a negative and statistically significant effect on investment policy, both partially (coefficient = −0.1602, p = 0.009) and in the full model (coefficient = −0.1464, p = 0.025). Financial market fluctuations are negative and significant when estimated separately (coefficient = −1.2011, p = 0.035) but become insignificant in the full model once oil price uncertainty is controlled for (coefficient = −0.2546, p = 0.679). ESG performance shows a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient across all specifications (full model: coefficient = 0.0003, p = 0.286). The full model yields a Wald χ² of 13.84 (p = 0.032) with an overall R² of 0.074. Conclusion: Oil price uncertainty is the most dominant and consistent factor constraining corporate investment among energy companies in ASEAN and East Asia, consistent with real options theory.

title: Board Heterogeneity and Market Risk on the Financial Performance of Listed Conglomerate Businesses in Nigeria
summary: The study examined the effect of board heterogeneity and market risk on the financial performance of listed conglomerate businesses in Nigeria. The study adopted a causal-comparative research design using secondary data obtained from the audited annual reports of the ten leading listed conglomerate businesses in Nigeria over the period 2015–2024. Panel data were analysed using descriptive statistics, diagnostic tests, and the Generalised Linear Model (GLM) at the 5 percent level of significance. The findings revealed that the nationality of board members had a positive but not statistically significant effect on financial performance (β = 0.0847, p = 0.7866), while equity price risk had a negative but not statistically significant effect on Earnings per Share (β = -0.0408, p = 0.5411). The study contributes to the corporate governance literature by integrating the Upper Echelons Theory and the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) to examine the combined influence of internal governance mechanisms and external market risk on financial performance.

title: Heritage Education, Arts-Based Learning, and Digital Transformation: A Systematic Review and Proposed Ecosystem Framework
summary: Heritage education has undergone substantial conceptual, pedagogical, and technological transformations over the last decade, driven by the expansion of digital technologies, participatory pedagogies, and arts-based approaches to learning. Although research in this field has grown considerably, existing studies remain fragmented across educational contexts, disciplinary traditions, and methodological perspectives. This systematic review aims to synthesise international research published between 2015 and 2026 on the relationships among heritage education, arts-based learning, museum education, digital transformation, sustainability, and teacher education. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 Statement and the PRISMA-S reporting recommendations. Searches conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus identified 525 records, of which 53 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. The findings reveal a marked expansion of museum-based and digitally mediated heritage learning, the growing adoption of arts-based pedagogies, and an increasing emphasis on teacher education and community participation. While digital technologies have become firmly established within heritage education, artificial intelligence remains an emerging area of inquiry with limited empirical evidence. The review also identifies persistent challenges, including the underrepresentation of rural and non-Western perspectives, limited longitudinal research, and the need for more robust methodological designs. Building on the synthesis of the reviewed literature, the article proposes the Arts-Based Heritage Learning Ecosystem as an integrative framework for understanding the interplay among cultural memory, artistic mediation, museum participation, digital innovation, sustainability, and teacher education. The study contributes to current debates by providing an updated synthesis of international research and by offering a conceptual basis to inform future research, curriculum development, and educational practice.

title: Smart School Leadership in Resource-Constrained Primary Education: An Empirical Case Study of Digital Transformation
summary: The evolution of educational technology requires primary school leaders to navigate digital transformation, yet mainstream digital leadership frameworks often overlook the realities of under-resourced schools. This study investigates the operationalization of Smart School Leadership (SSL) within a resource-constrained primary school setting, examining how school administrators adapt leadership practices amid material and structural limitations. Employing a qualitative single-case study design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews, direct field observations, and institutional artifact analysis involving eight participants, including the school principal, instructional teachers, and administrative personnel at SD Negeri 1 Simbune, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using interactive qualitative condensation, thematic displays, and continuous verification. The findings reveal that SSL implementation operates through an adaptive, staged transition rather than a sudden digital overhaul. Leadership practices are strategically prioritized toward core administrative workflows, compliance database management, and basic data-driven decision-making to address foundational early-grade literacy and numeracy needs. Furthermore, internal social capital and informal distributed leadership structures, specifically peer-assisted mentoring led by tech-savvy junior educators, serve as critical compensatory mechanisms to bridge faculty digital literacy divides. However, persistent structural friction, including hardware scarcity, unstable internet connectivity, pedagogical inertia, and non-systemic external training programs, places a clear ceiling on advancing to fully integrated digital pedagogy. This study implies that policymakers must move beyond uniform technology mandates toward equity-focused infrastructure allocation and continuous, school-based professional development tailored to rural primary school contexts.

title: The Missing Column: measured institutional silence on men and boys in international accounting systems
summary: International development and equality institutions account for money by stated purpose rather than measured outcome, and their reporting systems contain no field recording who a project's beneficiary is, for either sex. With preregistered text censuses, replicated controls and a public correction log, this paper measures what that architecture produces for men and boys. Findings. A purpose ledger of USD 71.8 billion a year beside a structurally uncountable men-and-boys series (the marker system's own handbook: the marker "cannot and does not intend to measure the outcome or impact"). A measured male beneficiary class that is nearly empty at record level: zero of Norway's 7,270 aid rows aimed at men's own outcomes; a global class dominated by a single procedure; fifty recorded dollars in the IATI register against the exploitation of boys in Thailand. Text corpora running sixteen to nineteen times above a replicated sector baseline (UN Women 320 girls-only publications against 4 boys-only; WHO 4.23:1 and World Bank 5.00:1 under identical preregistered rules). 24,043 words of UN child-justice guidance without the word boys, for a detained population the UN itself counts as 94 per cent male. Funding censuses across 25 funders at near parity in biomedicine (1.07:1) and four against 144 in participation programmes. A six-link institutional chain (finding, owner, indicator, budget, report, accountability) fully named for women and girls and empty from link two onward. A national deep case (Norway) reaching a directorate function of NOK 721.6 million whose equality share is unmeasurable in the state's own documents. Method and credibility. Rules were fixed before results; two of the project's own measures were killed by their own controls and are published as withdrawn; one preregistered experiment disconfirmed and is published as designed; the public correction log has cut against the project's own thesis, dated. All 172 factual assertions in the paper were independently audited before deposit; the audit ships inside the paper as Appendix A and beside it as claims-table.csv, built for row-by-row spot-checking. What this paper does not claim. No motive or intent of any institution. No causation from the correlations in its context sections. Nothing against UN Women: the machinery that exists is conceded as real, funded and effective, and its results are used as evidence the model works. The argument is for a second column in the same ledger, not a smaller first column. title: FUNCTIONS OF REMUNERATION IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR AS AN ACCOUNTING CATEGORY
summary: The article examines the functions of remuneration in the public sector as an accounting category, taking into account its economic essence and the specific features of its functioning as an object of accounting in public sector institutions. The study substantiates the need to expand traditional approaches to defining the functions of remuneration by integrating economic, social, and accounting and managerial dimensions into its analysis. An analysis of scholarly approaches to the functions of wages and accounting has revealed the absence of a unified classification framework and has justified the expediency of distinguishing the functions of remuneration from the perspective of the subject area of accounting in public sector institutions. The study proposes a systematisation of remuneration functions into two interrelated groups: economic and social functions, and accounting and managerial functions. The first group includes reproductive, social, incentive (motivational), regulatory, and distributive functions, which reflect the role of remuneration within the system of social and labour relations. The second group comprises informational, control, managerial, and analytical functions, as well as the functions of ensuring transparency and accountability and ensuring compliance, which characterise remuneration as an independent object of accounting in public sector institutions. It is demonstrated that the proposed approach provides a comprehensive understanding of the role of remuneration in public financial management, internal control, public sector auditing, and the transparent and efficient use of budgetary resources. The classification of payroll functions into distinct groups facilitates meeting the information needs of users in the context of reforms to the remuneration system in public sector institutions. The proposed classification of remuneration functions contributes to the further development of the theoretical foundations of remuneration accounting in the public sector and enhances the information support of managerial and control processes within public sector institutions.

title: Time-Consistent Investment Strategies for Relative Investment Games Under Ambiguity Aversion
summary: With the increasing power of institutional investors, in order to compete for more investment agency business, the competition among institutional investors has become increasingly fierce. This paper studies a non-zero-sum game between two competing institutional investors who adopt mean–variance preferences and account for model uncertainty in order to derive robust optimal portfolios. The ambiguity-averse institutional investors can invest in a financial market with one risk-free bond and one individual stock. The objective of each institutional investor is to maximize the mean–variance utility of his terminal wealth relative to that of his competitor under the worst-case scenario of the alternative measures. By means of stochastic dynamic programming, we obtain closed-form expressions for the robust Nash equilibrium strategies and prove a verification theorem. Numerical simulations are finally presented to examine how model parameters influence the equilibrium strategies and to extract associated economic interpretations.

title: Intellectual drivers of AI adoption maturity and its domino effect on ethical AI governance and open green innovation
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the potential role of intellectual capital dimensions on artificial intelligence (AI) adoption maturity in the Jordanian pharmaceutical industry. It also explores the contribution of this maturity to the formation of ethical AI governance and open green innovation (OGI). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 16 pharmaceutical manufacturing companies. The Smart PLS program was used to analyze 257 responses from managers and AI specialists. Findings The results revealed that intellectual capital, encompassing human, structural and social components, has a significant impact on AI adoption maturity. The results also indicated that AI adoption maturity significantly impacts ethical AI governance and OGI. Furthermore, it was found that ethical AI governance partially mediates the role of AI adoption maturity in OGI. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, the current empirical study represents the first attempt to outline the consistent framework of intellectual capital, maturity of AI adoption, AI-ethical governance and open-green innovation in a new and integrated environment. What makes it novel and unique is that it does not just examine the individual effects of these variables but it analyzes their dynamic interaction and how they can jointly contribute to institutional maturity in adopting AI and how they can contribute to sustainable and ethical results at the organizational level. In addition, it opens new sources of studying the ways in which organizations can take AI-based opportunities to develop ethical and sustainable innovation, which is an area with little empirical research. The study, therefore, presents a new scientific input, as well as practical solutions that can be used to promote sustainable and ethical innovation in the modern business environment.
